questions.stem: When ethene reacts with steam (H₂O) in the presence of a phosphoric acid catalyst at high temperature and pressure, what is the product?

options.text: Ethane
Ethanoic acid
Ethanol
Ethane-1,2-diol

questions.explanation: This is an addition reaction: steam (H₂O) adds across the C=C double bond of ethene. The H adds to one carbon and the OH adds to the other, producing ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH). This is called hydration and is the main industrial method for producing ethanol. The reaction is: C₂H₄ + H₂O → C₂H₅OH.

questions.stem: Propene reacts with hydrogen bromide (HBr). What type of reaction is this, and what is the main organic product?

options.text: Substitution reaction; 1-bromopropane
Addition reaction; 2-bromopropane
Combustion; carbon dioxide and water
Elimination reaction; propyne

questions.explanation: Alkenes undergo addition reactions where atoms add across the C=C double bond. HBr adds across propene's double bond. The bromine preferentially bonds to the middle carbon (following Markovnikov's rule at higher level), producing 2-bromopropane as the main product: CH₃CH=CH₂ + HBr → CH₃CHBrCH₃.

questions.stem: Ethene reacts with bromine water and the orange colour disappears. A student writes: C₂H₄ + Br₂ → C₂H₄Br₂. What is the name of this product and what has happened to the double bond?

options.text: Ethanol; the double bond became a triple bond
1,2-dibromoethane; the double bond opened up to form single bonds as bromine atoms added across it
Bromoethane; only one bromine atom added
Ethane; the bromine acted as a catalyst

questions.explanation: The product is 1,2-dibromoethane (CH₂BrCH₂Br). The C=C double bond breaks open — one bond of the double bond breaks while the other remains as a single bond. Each bromine atom bonds to one of the carbon atoms. This is why it is called an addition reaction: atoms are added and no atoms are lost.

questions.stem: Margarine is made by reacting vegetable oils (which contain C=C double bonds) with hydrogen using a nickel catalyst at about 60°C. What type of reaction is this and how does it change the oil?

options.text: Combustion; it breaks down the oil molecules
Hydrogenation (addition of hydrogen); it converts unsaturated C=C bonds to saturated C-C bonds, hardening the oil
Neutralisation; it removes acids from the oil
Cracking; it breaks the oil into smaller molecules

questions.explanation: This is hydrogenation — an addition reaction where hydrogen adds across C=C double bonds, converting them to single bonds. This makes the molecules more saturated, which increases the melting point and turns the liquid oil into a solid or semi-solid fat (margarine). A nickel catalyst is needed to make the reaction happen at a reasonable temperature.

questions.stem: Many ethene molecules can join together in an addition polymerisation reaction. What happens to the C=C double bonds during this process?

options.text: They remain as double bonds in the polymer chain
They break completely and the carbon atoms separate
One bond of each double bond opens up, linking monomers together in a long chain with only single C-C bonds
They become triple bonds to hold the chain together more strongly

questions.explanation: In addition polymerisation, one bond of each C=C double bond in the monomer opens up. These opened bonds link to the adjacent monomers, forming a long chain held together by single C-C bonds. The polymer poly(ethene) — commonly known as polyethylene — has no double bonds remaining in its backbone. This is why only unsaturated monomers (with C=C bonds) can undergo addition polymerisation.
